title: Logical Jobs and Fallback Graphs
summary: A logical job represents a business obligation that may be fulfilled by one or more implementation stages.
why: Allows a conversation to move from a cheap script to an expensive LLM (Gemma -> Grok -> OpenAI) while remaining under one business budget.
invariants: A logical job has one parent budget lease.
Each implementation stage receives a child WLUReservation, not the whole parent budget.
Fallback branches are alternatives; the strategy ceiling is the maximum of the current stage plus the maximum successor path, not the sum.
A budget may admit a job with a 'PARTIAL_STRATEGY' if the total budget is less than the full fallback graph but fits the current path.
evidence_note: Source: oorexx_work_load_units_v0.12/README.md:150-175. Line 152: 'One chat/session may legitimately move through several execution implementations while remaining one WLU budget.'
